## Developer Tools / Dependency Security Advisories

Find published security advisories for identifiable software packages and interpret their affected and fixed versions.

**Includes:** Retrieves identifiable public advisories using a package ecosystem, package name, version or advisory identifier, with source links and affected-version or remediation metadata where available.

**Boundary:** Source-code analysis, exploit execution, infrastructure scanning and discovering previously unknown vulnerabilities are separate. A successful lookup or no match does not establish that software is secure, exploitable in a particular application, or free of other vulnerabilities. Aggregators can share upstream records; matching answers are not independent security findings.

## Search & Data Access / Scholarly Literature Search

Find identifiable scholarly works and their bibliographic metadata from publication clues or research queries.

**Includes:** Searches an identifiable scholarly corpus and returns work identities with citation metadata such as title, authors, publication venue, year and persistent identifiers where available.

**Boundary:** General web-page search, guaranteed full-text access, literature-review synthesis and research-quality rankings are separate. Corpus coverage and identifier availability vary; citation counts or agreement between indexes do not independently establish a paper's identity, quality or completeness.

The optional polite pool has 3 list requests/second, 10 single-record requests/second and concurrency 3. Follow response limit headers, cache results, identify the application and back off on 429 or increasing response time. A real email is recommended for contact, not a new account; polite limits are shared by that email. Almost all bibliographic metadata may be reused for any purpose, but abstracts can retain publisher/author copyright. Metadata access does not grant full-text rights. No explicit public comparison prohibition was found in the reviewed retrieval/access policies. These documented categories are not a guarantee that every identifier-based request consumes zero allowance. Thus the anonymous budget covers about 100 plain searches if used for nothing else. Response headers and meta report actual usage; the quota's anonymous sharing scope was not specified in the reviewed pages. A free account raises the daily allowance to $1 with no payment method; that optional keyed route has not been registered or tested here. More than 100 requests/second or budget exhaustion triggers 429; use backoff. API pages return at most 100 results each. Official metadata is released under CC0; abstracts and linked full texts can involve third-party rights, and a paper's availability is not permission to republish it. Reviewed terms contain no explicit public-benchmark ban; access abuse, bypassing restrictions and misleading trademark use remain restricted. Crossref is one upstream source, so agreement with Crossref is not independent confirmation. No business API query was made for this source review. | [scholarly-access-001: completed (2026-10-08)](../data/experiments/evaluations/openalex-scholarly-access-ds41-r1.json); [scholarly-reference-001: completed (2026-10-08)](../data/experiments/evaluations/openalex-scholarly-reference-001-ds41-r1.json) |

<a id="web-search-data-geocoding"></a>

## Search & Data Access / Geocoding

Resolve named places or supplied public addresses to geographic coordinates.

**Includes:** Returns a geographic position with enough place or address context to identify the match; coverage, result granularity and public-endpoint conditions must be specified.

**Boundary:** General web search, weather at known coordinates, map tiles and route navigation are separate. A place or building coordinate does not establish an exact entrance, postal deliverability or safe navigation to a destination.



| Service | Classification | Route | Data kind | Availability | Personal access | Requirements, published costs and limits | Observed tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Geoapify](../data/candidates/geoapify.yaml) | web-search-data/geocoding | [geocoding-api (api)](https://api.geoapify.com/v1/geocode/search) | unknown | self_serve | documented | Requires: platform_account; 3000 credits / day (free_allowance; Free plan; a standard forward-geocoding request costs one credit. Other APIs can share credits and use different credit costs.); Human: Register an email/password account, complete the normal verification flow and create a Free project in MyProjects; an API key is generated for the project.; Free plan supports up to 5 requests/second. Registration documentation names Google reCAPTCHA; phone requirements and acceptance of a particular email domain were not observed. An official API key is required for integration; the public playground is not an anonymous production route. Terms version 5 dated 2024-02-02 prohibits overload, access-control bypass and distributing usage across accounts/projects to evade limits. No explicit public-benchmark prohibition was found in the reviewed terms. Free use requires Geoapify attribution and OSM attribution; preserve any additional returned data-source attribution. Results may be stored with attribution, according to the geocoding FAQ. Shared OSM inputs do not constitute independent geographic ground truth. Controller preparation observation on 2026-10-09 (Asia/Shanghai), separate from official-source claims and any formal trial: the email form was not submitted. <a id="productivity-storage-qr-codes"></a>

## Productivity & Collaboration / QR Code Images

Create a reusable static QR code image that encodes supplied text or a link for sharing or printing.

**Includes:** A hosted service accepts an explicit payload and returns a downloadable QR image with documented format and sizing controls. The stored payload can be checked by an independent decoder; local-only encoding libraries are not hosted service alternatives.

**Boundary:** Payment processing, scanner-only services, dynamic redirect or scan-tracking management and general AI image generation are separate. An image that looks like a QR code without correctly decoding the requested payload is insufficient; decoding does not prove its destination is safe, reachable or permanent, or that every phone and print condition can scan it.
